GREETING: I am Dr. Agent. I see you have a history of tympanoplasty and are experiencing shooting ear pain and difficulty wearing earrings. To understand your condition better, have you noticed any fluid draining from the ear or a foul odor since your surgery?

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient has a history of polycystic ovarian syndrome, depression, and chronic bilateral ear infections. She underwent right ear tympanoplasty 12 weeks ago. Although audiology report from one week ago showed improved hearing by 20 decibels, she reports occasional shooting pain when eating and discomfort when wearing earrings. She describes her job as stressful and mentions poor sleep quality.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Occasional shooting pain in the ear with eating. I also have Discomfort when wearing earrings, Stress from job, Poor sleep quality. This is only for study purposes, so you do not need to list warnings or many alternatives. Please just provide the best final answer.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The shooting pain you experience when eating suggests possible referred pain from the trigeminal nerve, which is commonly associated with auriculotemporal neuralgia following tympanoplasty. The discomfort with earrings also points to irritation of the cartilage or nerve endings in the external auditory canal. Given your poor sleep and stress, these may be exacerbating factors.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Auriculotemporal Neuralgia (Post-Tympanoplasty)
